```{r}
#get rid of unknown value in race column 
data <- read.csv("../../data/cleaning/null_demographics_removed.csv")
#check columns 
#head(data)
#check how many unknowns pre removing unknowns
#sum(data$susp_race == "UNKNOWN", na.rm = TRUE)

#remove unknowns 
data <- data[data$susp_race != "UNKNOWN", ]
sum(data$susp_race == "UNKNOWN", na.rm = TRUE)

head(data)
nrow(data)
```

```{r}
# Get the top 20 precincts by crime count
top_precincts_table <- data %>%
  count(precinct_crime, sort = TRUE) %>%    # count crimes per precinct
  slice_max(n, n = 20) %>%                  # keep top 20
  arrange(precinct_crime)                   # sort ascending

print(top_precincts_table)

# Turn that table into a simple vector of precinct IDs
top_precincts <- top_precincts_table$precinct_crime

# Filter main data to only those top 20 precincts
df_tp_race <- data %>%
  filter(precinct_crime %in% top_precincts)

# Vector of precincts we'll loop over
precincts <- sort(unique(df_tp_race$precinct_crime))
precincts
```

```{r}
# 2. Run chi-square tests for race x time_period in each precinct
race_chi_results <- tibble()

for (p in precincts) {
  # Subset to this precinct
  df_p <- df_tp_race %>%
    filter(precinct_crime == p)
  
  # Contingency table: race × time_period
  tab <- table(df_p$susp_race, df_p$time_period)
  
  # Skip if table is degenerate (e.g., only one row/column)
  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) next
  
  # Chi-square test
  chi <- chisq.test(tab)
  
  # Store results
  race_chi_results <- race_chi_results %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(
      precinct_crime = p,
      statistic      = as.numeric(chi$statistic),
      p_value        = chi$p.value,
      df             = as.numeric(chi$parameter)
    ))
}

race_chi_results

#write.csv(race_chi_results,
#          "race_precinct_chi_results.csv",
#          row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
# 3. Precincts with statistically significant race distribution change
sig_race_chi_results <- race_chi_results %>%
  filter(p_value < 0.05)

sig_race_chi_results

sig_race_chi_precincts <- sig_race_chi_results %>%
  distinct(precinct_crime) %>%
  pull()

sig_race_chi_precincts

#write.csv(sig_race_chi_precincts,
#          "race_precinct_chi_result_significant.csv",
#          row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
# 4a. Post-hoc standardized residuals for each cell (race x time_period)
race_posthoc_results <- tibble()

for (p in precincts) {
  
  df_p <- df_tp_race %>%
    filter(precinct_crime == p)
  
  tab <- table(df_p$susp_race, df_p$time_period)
  
  # Skip if not a proper 2D table
  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) next
  
  chi <- chisq.test(tab)
  
  # Standardized residuals matrix
  resid_mat <- chi$stdres
  
  # Tidy version
  resid_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(resid_mat)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    rename(
      susp_race    = Var1,
      time_period  = Var2,
      std_residual = Freq
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      precinct_crime = p,
      chi_statistic  = as.numeric(chi$statistic),
      p_value        = chi$p.value
    )
  
  race_posthoc_results <- race_posthoc_results %>%
    bind_rows(resid_df)
}

race_posthoc_results

#write.csv(race_posthoc_results,
#          "race_chi_posthoc_results.csv",
#          row.names = FALSE)


sorted_residuals <- race_posthoc_results |>
  arrange(desc(abs(std_residual)))

print(sorted_residuals)
```

```{r}
#4. Before/after shift in standardized residuals (by race)
race_shift_results <- race_posthoc_results %>%
  select(precinct_crime, susp_race, time_period, std_residual) %>%
  mutate(
    time_period = ifelse(time_period == "before Patternizr", "before", "after")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = time_period,
    values_from = std_residual
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    shift = after - before   # positive = more overrepresented after
  )

# Large positive shifts
race_shift_results %>% filter(shift > 2)

# Large negative shifts
race_shift_results %>% filter(shift < -2)

race_shift_results %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(shift))) %>%
  head(20)

```
